intent: Static helpers for reading, merging, stripping, and sanitizing JSON::Value trees (key replace/strip/patch, path<->object conversion, transport-safe string sanitizing) used across Bedrock and consuming applications.

objects.name: Utils
objects.role: static utility class holding shared singleton JSON::Value constants and tree-manipulation helpers; no instance state

objects.name: Utils::EMPTY_OBJECT/EMPTY_ARRAY/NULL_VALUE/FALSE_VALUE/TRUE_VALUE/EMPTY_STRING/ZERO_INT_VALUE/MAX_INT_VALUE/ZERO_FLOAT_VALUE
objects.role: shared singleton JSON::Value constants reused to avoid repeated construction

objects.name: Utils::sanitizeJSONStringForTransport
objects.role: hand-rolled UTF-8 validator/control-byte stripper for outbound JSON strings

misfits.why: doc comment is written entirely in terms of one caller's domain (bankAccounts.additionalData, apiResult, errorAttemptsCount, assetReport) and names an external test (GetWithdrawalAccountsTest) not present in this repo; the algorithm is generic but the documentation ties a package the README describes as application-agnostic to one consumer's onyx-merge use case

name_fit.note: generic JSON-tree utility grab-bag fits its name

naming_quality.note: clear camelCase methods; class name Utils is a generic catch-all but scoped under JSON:: so it doesn't collide with the repo's S-prefixed shared-utility convention

intent: A JSON serializer: build a document incrementally via an object/array cursor over rapidjson::Writer, or convert a whole JSON::Value tree to a string in one call (compact or pretty).

objects.name: Writer
objects.role: wraps rapidjson::Writer<StringBuffer>; instance API drives incremental construction, static serialize()/serializePretty() walk an existing JSON::Value tree directly

objects.name: Writer::serialize(value, writer)
objects.role: recursively walks a JSON::Value and feeds it to any rapidjson writer type; shared by serialize() and serializePretty()

naming_quality.note: consistent startX/endX pairs; private writeValue overloads appropriately hidden behind public templates

intent: Implements rapidjson's SAX handler interface to build a JSON::Value tree (with nested objects/arrays) from the callback stream a rapidjson::Reader emits while parsing.

objects.name: SAXHandler
objects.role: implements the full rapidjson handler surface (Null/Bool/Int/Uint/Int64/Uint64/Double/String/StartObject/Key/EndObject/StartArray/EndArray/RawNumber), tracks a stack of in-progress Value contexts, hands off the finished root via getValue()

objects.name: SAXHandler::endContext
objects.role: pops the current context and, inside an array, stages the next placeholder element

name_fit.note: matches the rapidjson SAX handler convention it implements

naming_quality.note: interface names are fixed by rapidjson's contract; root is a manually new/deleted raw pointer later wrapped in a unique_ptr on hand-off, an ownership pattern worth a second look though not a naming issue

intent: Parse a JSON string into a JSON::Value tree, in a strict mode that throws on malformed input and a permissive mode that does not.

objects.name: Parser
objects.role: two static entry points, read() (throws JSON::InvalidArgument) and readUnsafe() (swallows parse errors), both driving a rapidjson::Reader over a SAXHandler

naming_quality.note: readUnsafe clearly signals the risk relative to read

intent: A CRTP base that documents and compile-time-enforces a toJSON()/fromJSON() contract on a derived type, without a vtable, so the derived type stays an aggregate.

objects.name: Serializable<Derived>
objects.role: base toJSON()/fromJSON() are static_assert stubs that fire only if the derived class fails to hide them via name hiding

objects.name: always_false_v<T>
objects.role: delays the static_assert failure to instantiation time

location_fit.note: a JSON-serialization contract helper, reasonably grouped here even though the CRTP trick itself is generic C++, not JSON-specific; no in-repo consumer currently derives from it

naming_quality.note: always_false_v follows established standard-library-style naming for this trait helper

intent: A narrow, process-wide hook so an embedding application can observe JSON parse/serialize timing and document size, without the JSON package depending on that application.

objects.name: setMetricsObserver
objects.role: installs/replaces the callback; nullptr disables reporting

objects.name: reportMetrics
objects.role: invoked by Parser/Writer after each operation to notify the observer, if set

objects.name: (anonymous namespace) metricsObserver
objects.role: atomic<MetricsObserver> backing storage; not declared in the header
